title: The embryonic period

objective.text: Explain why the embryonic period matters so much for birth defects.

body.general: Why do the first two months of pregnancy matter so much? From week 3 to week 8, each of the three cell layers, the germ layers, builds its own tissues and organs [f1]. This stretch is the embryonic period, or embryogenesis, when organs form (organogenesis) [f1]. By its end, every main organ system exists and the body looks human [f7]. So this is when most major birth defects begin [f3]. Harmful agents, teratogens, do most damage now [f4]. Weeks 3 and 4 carry special risk, often before a woman knows she is pregnant [f5].
body.mbbs: The embryonic period, embryogenesis proper, runs from week 3 to week 8 after fertilization [f1]. In it each germ layer gives rise to its own tissues and organs (organogenesis) [f1]. By the end of month 2 the main organ systems are laid down and the external form is recognisable [f7]. At the end of week 8 the crown–rump length is about 28–30 mm [f2]. Most major structural birth defects arise in this window, so it is the period most sensitive to teratogens [f3,f4]. An insult in weeks 1–2 more often ends the pregnancy than causes a malformation [f6]. Weeks 3–4 are especially vulnerable and often pass before the pregnancy is recognised [f5].

facts.text: From week 3 to week 8 each germ layer builds its own tissues and organs.
By the end of month 2 the main organ systems exist and the outer body form is recognisable.
facts.note: R02: over 90 % of named adult structures present at CS23

facts.text: At the end of week 8 the embryo's crown–rump length is about 28–30 mm.
Most major structural birth defects arise during the embryonic period.
Because organs are forming, weeks 3 to 8 are the time most sensitive to teratogens.
Weeks 3 and 4 are especially vulnerable, and often pass before a woman knows she is pregnant.
Before the embryonic period, a serious insult usually ends the pregnancy rather than causing a malformation.

misconceptions.wrong: The most dangerous time for teratogens is late pregnancy.
misconceptions.right: The most sensitive time is weeks 3 to 8, while the organs are forming.

misconceptions.wrong: Harm in the first two weeks causes most malformations.
misconceptions.right: A serious insult before week 3 usually ends the pregnancy; malformations mostly start in weeks 3 to 8.

checks.prompt: When do most major structural birth defects begin?
checks.why: Weeks 3 to 8 are when the organs form, so that is when most major defects arise.

checks.prompt: A serious insult hits in week 2. What is the most usual result?
options: A defect that shows only after birth
checks.why: Before the embryonic period a serious insult usually ends the pregnancy rather than causing a malformation.

checks.prompt: Why are weeks 3 and 4 a special worry?
options: The placenta is not yet attached
Organs form before many women know they are pregnant
The embryo grows fastest in length then
The germ layers have not formed yet
checks.why: Organ building starts in weeks 3–4, often before the pregnancy is recognised, so exposures can go unnoticed.

adult: By week 8 the plan of every adult organ system is already in place [f7].
clinical: Weeks 3 and 4 often pass before a pregnancy is recognised [f5]. So harmful exposures in this window can happen unnoticed [f4,f5].

remember.q: Which weeks make up the embryonic period?
remember.a: Weeks 3 to 8, when each germ layer builds its tissues and organs [f1].

remember.q: Why is the embryonic period the riskiest time for teratogens?
remember.a: Organs are forming, so most major structural birth defects arise then [f3,f4].

remember.q: What usually follows a serious insult before week 3?
remember.a: Loss of the pregnancy rather than a malformation [f6].
